This passage is from **Homer’s *Iliad* (Book 19, lines 184–197)**, in which Agamemnon responds to Odysseus after Odysseus has successfully negotiated the return of Briseis and the potential reconciliation with Achilles.

Here is the translation:

***

And Agamemnon, lord of men, spoke to him in turn:
"I rejoice, son of Laertes, to hear your words,
for you have gone through everything in due measure and recounted it well.
These things I am willing to swear—my own heart commands me—
and I shall not swear falsely before the gods. But let Achilles
remain here for a while, even though he is eager for battle;
and let all you others remain gathered here, until the gifts
come forth from my hut and we strike faithful oaths.
And to you yourself I give this charge and command:
Select the most excellent youths of all the Achaeans
to bring from my ship the gifts which we promised Achilles
yesterday that we would give, and lead forth the women.
And let Talthybius swiftly prepare for me, throughout the wide camp of the Achaeans,
a boar to sacrifice to Zeus and to Helios."

***

### Notes on the translation:
*   **"Lord of men" (ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν):** A standard Homeric epithet for Agamemnon.
*   **"In due measure" (ἐν μοίρῃ):** Meaning Odysseus spoke with propriety, logic, and fairness.
*   **"Strike faithful oaths" (ὅρκια πιστὰ τάμωμεν):** Literally "cut faithful oaths." In ancient Greece, oaths were accompanied by animal sacrifice; the act of "cutting" the throat of the animal symbolized what the gods should do to the oath-breaker.
*   **"Youths" (κούρητας):** Specifically, young men or warriors (often associated with the Kuretes, but used here in the general sense of "select young nobles/warriors").
*   **"Zeus and Helios":** Agamemnon calls specifically upon Zeus and the Sun-god (Helios) as the great witnesses who observe all things on earth and punish those who break solemn oaths.

τὸν δ᾽ αὖτε προσέειπεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων:
‘185χαίρω σεῦ Λαερτιάδη τὸν μῦθον ἀκούσας:
ἐν μοίρῃ γὰρ πάντα διίκεο καὶ κατέλεξας.
ταῦτα δ᾽ ἐγὼν ἐθέλω ὀμόσαι, κέλεται δέ με θυμός,
οὐδ᾽ ἐπιορκήσω πρὸς δαίμονος. αὐτὰρ Ἀχιλλεὺς
μιμνέτω αὐτόθι τεῖος ἐπειγόμενός περ Ἄρηος:
190μίμνετε δ᾽ ἄλλοι πάντες ἀολλέες, ὄφρά κε δῶρα
ἐκ κλισίης ἔλθῃσι καὶ ὅρκια πιστὰ τάμωμεν.
σοὶ δ᾽ αὐτῷ τόδ᾽ ἐγὼν ἐπιτέλλομαι ἠδὲ κελεύω:
κρινάμενος κούρητας ἀριστῆας Παναχαιῶν
δῶρα ἐμῆς παρὰ νηὸς ἐνεικέμεν, ὅσσ᾽ Ἀχιλῆϊ
195χθιζὸν ὑπέστημεν δώσειν, ἀγέμεν τε γυναῖκας.
Ταλθύβιος δέ μοι ὦκα κατὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν
κάπρον ἑτοιμασάτω ταμέειν Διί τ᾽ Ἠελίῳ τε.
